nodes.label: Composition Root
nodes.rationale: The single place in the application where concrete objects are created and wired together, keeping business classes free of direct instantiation of concrete dependencies.

nodes.label: Dependency Injection (DI)
nodes.rationale: Passing an object its dependencies instead of letting it construct them itself; in Python, manual constructor injection in the composition root is usually enough and avoids the overhead of a container.

nodes.label: Dependency Inversion Principle
nodes.rationale: High-level and low-level modules both depend on an abstraction; the concrete dependency is injected from outside so the business rule is not tied to a technical detail like SQL.

nodes.label: Interface Segregation Principle
nodes.rationale: No class should be forced to implement methods it does not use; split one large interface into small cohesive ones per capability.

nodes.label: Inversion of Control (IoC)
nodes.rationale: Delegating creation and injection of dependencies to a container/framework; worthwhile only when the dependency graph grows large enough that manual DI becomes unwieldy.

nodes.label: Liskov Substitution Principle
nodes.rationale: Subtypes must be usable wherever the base type is expected without the client checking isinstance; solved via Tell, Don't Ask so each subtype resolves its own behavior.

nodes.label: Open/Closed Principle
nodes.rationale: New variants should be new classes implementing a shared interface, not new branches in an existing if/elif, to avoid regressions in already-tested code; apply only when variation is real or highly likely, not speculatively.

nodes.label: Protocol vs ABC for behavior contracts
nodes.norm_label: protocol vs abc for behavior contracts
nodes.rationale: Protocol does not force inheritance and suits new contracts; ABC + @abstractmethod prevents instantiating an incomplete implementation or lets the base share code. Both are valid; the repo's own examples use ABC while the prescriptive templates prefer Protocol. Note: mypy rejects passing an ABC where type[T] is expected (mypy#4717), so pyproject.toml disables the type-abstract check.

nodes.label: Single Responsibility Principle
nodes.rationale: Each class has one reason to change; splitting persistence/calculation out of domain data avoids forcing unrelated changes to ripple into the entity.

nodes.label: Tell, Don't Ask
nodes.rationale: Ask the object to do something instead of querying its type/state and deciding externally; this is the mechanism that fixes Liskov substitution violations caused by isinstance checks.

nodes.label: Cohesion
nodes.rationale: The degree to which the parts of a software component relate to each other; high cohesion is desirable.

nodes.label: Coupling
nodes.rationale: The level of dependency between software components; low coupling is desirable.

nodes.label: SOLID (overarching concept)
nodes.rationale: The five principles are intertwined and interdependent; they are most effective applied together rather than in isolation.
